title: Familiar verbs with plural partitive
summary: Choose plural partitive objects with the familiar waiting, helping and listening patterns.
objectives: Choose plural partitive objects with the familiar waiting, helping and listening patterns.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Choose plural partitive objects with the familiar waiting, helping and listening patterns.
Object number is independent of the person doing the action. One speaker can help several people. Keep the supplied verb form and choose the plural object.
The complete plural forms are supplied, including changing forms. Their full formation systems are outside this usage lesson.
keyPoints: In the ordinary waiting, helping and listening meanings taught here, several people or things use a plural partitive object.

steps: In the ordinary waiting, helping and listening meanings taught here, several people or things use a plural partitive object.
Odotan means “I am waiting for” and works as the verb. odotan comes from odottaa: odota- + -n, with tt → t.
busseja means “buses” and works as the plural partitive noun used as the object of the action. Change final i to e, then add -ja: busse- + -ja = busseja.
In the ordinary waiting, helping and listening meanings taught here, several people or things use a plural partitive object.
Odotan means “I am waiting for” and works as the verb. odotan comes from odottaa: odota- + -n, with tt → t.
junia means “trains” and works as the plural partitive noun used as the object of the action. Replace final a with plural i, then add -a: jun-i-a = junia.
In the ordinary waiting, helping and listening meanings taught here, several people or things use a plural partitive object.
Autan means “I help” and works as the verb. autan comes from auttaa: auta- + -n, with tt → t.
ystäviä means “friends” and works as the plural partitive noun used as the object of the action. Replace final ä with plural i, then add -ä: ystäv-i-ä = ystäviä.
In the ordinary waiting, helping and listening meanings taught here, several people or things use a plural partitive object.
Kuuntelen means “I am listening to” and works as the verb. kuuntelen comes from kuunnella: kuuntele- + -n, with nn → nt and the e stem.
opettajia means “teachers” and works as the plural partitive noun used as the object of the action. Replace final a with plural i, then add -a: opettaj-i-a = opettajia.

commonMistakes: One speaker does not require a singular object.
Keep the partitive case when the object refers to several people.
